newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-MCGRATH DROPPED AS RIFT WITH VILLA WIDENS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MCGRATH DROPPED AS RIFT WITH VILLA WIDENS.

text.p: Ireland international Paul McGrath's long and successful career at Aston Villa appeared in tatters on Monday following a row with manager Brian Little.
McGrath is unhappy at having been relegated to the substitutes' bench this season and told a local newspaper at the weekend he wanted to leave the premier league club.
In retaliation, Little dropped the 36-year-old defender from the squad to face Newcastle on Monday night.
"I have sent Paul home and he has not travelled with us to Newcastle," Little said.
"I told Paul the only way we could settle this was if I left him out of my first-team thinking altogether and I sent him home."
McGrath claims Villa are preventing him from moving to another club by demanding a fee for him.
Midlands rivals Coventry approached Villa regarding a possible transfer deal a fortnight ago but were put off by the 200,000 pounds ($310,000) asking price.
But Little defended his stance. "Can you name me another premier league club who would let one of their 18 first-team squad members go for nothing?" he asked.
McGrath said Villa's insistence on a 200,000 pound fee for a 36-year-old at the end of his career "was nothing short of disgraceful".

"I have shown loyalty throughout my career to Aston Villa but that loyalty is not being repaid," the former Manchester United defender said. "What angers me most is that the club seem intent on blocking any opportunity for me to go elsewhere."
